memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "In all the travels of the Israelites, whenever the cloud lifted from above the tabernacle, they would set out; but if the cloud did not lift, they did not set out - until the day it lifted. So the cloud of the Lord was over the tabernacle by day, and fire was in the cloud by night, in the sight of all the Israelites during all their travels." - Exod 40:36-38 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The book of Exodus closes not with arrival but with travel. They were not yet in the promised land. They were still in a desert, still walking, still years from home.

But they were not walking alone.

Cloud by day, fire by night, visible to everyone, through all their journeys. God's guidance was not reserved for Moses; it was "in the sight of all the Israelites."

Notice the rhythm: when the cloud lifted, they moved. When it stayed, they stayed. Sometimes for a night, sometimes for months (Num 9:22). Following God meant being willing both to go and to wait — and waiting is often harder.

Many of us finish a season of building and find ourselves still in the wilderness, still travelling. If that is you, this ending is for you. Exodus does not conclude with everything resolved. It concludes with God's presence going with His people through what remains.

Jesus promised the same: surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age (Matt 28:20). And His Spirit leads us still (Rom 8:14).

Egypt is behind. The land is ahead. And the God who dwells among His people goes with you every step between.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you more willing to move for God or to wait for Him?
2. Where do you need to know God is with you in an unfinished season?
3. Looking back, where has He guided you without your realising it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You go with me through every stage of the journey. Help me move when You move and wait when You wait. Amen.
